text:
elena: quick heads-up — rolled runtime v2.9.1 to canary pool c10 ~10:12Z. support ticket #4332: customer sees p99 jump ~600ms on small-chat endpoints (same model, short prompts).

deploy-bot: deployed runtime/v2.9.1 -> canary(c10) at 2026-03-16T10:12:08Z

raj: link to dashboards? want p95/p99 histograms and request mix.

sam: any kernel/scheduler changes in this build? last few rollouts touched the runtime scheduler.

elena: short summary: main change was scheduler weight tuning + small kvcache prefetch tweak. No model changes. Diff gist: https://gists.internal/runtime/4a7b

support-jen: customer repro steps attached in ticket: single-turn chat, 80-120 tokens, concurrency 8-12. They sent sample curl: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"model":"open-lite-1","input":"hey"}'
```
They see ~180ms -> ~780ms p99 spike starting at 10:15Z.

ash: can we confirm whether kvcache hit rate changed? maybe prefetch causes cold evictions under this workload.

raj: grabbing metrics: https://metrics.internal/redwood/canary/4950012345 (p95 steady, p99 tail shifted upward). queueing percentiles show a small bump in request queue time for c10 nodes.

sam: if queueing bump + scheduler tweak — suspect weighted scheduler causing uneven bursts on hot shards. Can we try toggling scheduler back for a subset?

elena: plan: split canary c10 by 50/50 traffic (current v2.9.1 vs v2.9.1-sched-off) and observe p99s. can someone run the split and perf-check?

ash: running split now — command: `./tools/canary-split --pool c10 --weights 50,50 --variants v2.9.1,v2.9.1-sched-off`

oncall-bot: canary-split started at 2026-03-16T10:22Z (op id a3f9).

raj: early numbers: variant v2.9.1 p99 = ~720ms, variant v2.9.1-sched-off p99 = ~210ms. p95 similar across both. Looks like scheduler change is correlated to tail.

sam: nice isolate. can we reproduce locally with small driver? run load against single instance with scheduler enabled/disabled.

elena: repro in staging: single instance test shows same effect under concurrency 8-12. attaching minimal repro script: 
```
# runloader.sh
for i in {1..200}; do curl -sS -X POST $ENDPOINT -d '{"input":"ping"}' & done; wait
```

support-jen: forwarded to customer — they confirmed their side sees improvement when routed to sched-off variant.

ash: root cause hypothesis: weighted scheduler introduced micro-bursts on particular worker threads leading to queueing + larger serialize waits for small requests. p99 sensitive, p95 not much.

sam: mitigation options: 
- rollback scheduler tweak from canary (fast)
- add runtime fallback to round-robin when queueing > threshold (medium)
- add canary gating in CI for p99 under small-chat synthetic workload (longer)

elena: initiating rollback of scheduler change for canary now.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated: reverting scheduler weights in runtime v2.9.2-hotfix -> canary(c10) at 2026-03-16T10:38Z (op id b4c2).

raj: after rollback p99 on canary back to ~200-230ms within one minute.

support-jen: customer confirmed reduced latency on their side too. they asked for ETA on fix being promoted to prod.

elena: immediate next steps: 1) keep scheduler tweak disabled, 2) create ENGRT ticket with bisect results and add a gating test, 3) pair with runtime team to design safer rollout pattern (gradual weight ramp + p99 checks). Filing ENGRT-8921 now.

sam: add test: synthetic small-chat p99 < 300ms under concurrency 10 in canary gate. Also bump observability to include scheduler metrics.

elena: thanks all. adding postmortem placeholder and assigning owners. :thumbsup:

support-jen: noted — I'll update the customer with the rollback and share ETA when we have PR timeline. :white_check_mark:

ash: leaving notes in the diff: avoid weight jumps, add threshold-based fallback.

elena: filing postmortem + linking ticket here when ready. closing thread for now unless anything else crops up. :wave:
